questions.text:
Wāhanga Tuatahi / Section One: He reta ki te Tumuaki — A letter to the Principal

A group of rangatahi at Te Pūriri College have decided to write to their principal to request that te reo Māori be used in all school announcements and signage. Senior students Wiremu and Kahu discuss the plan via text messages. They discuss reasons for bilingual signage, including normalising te reo in everyday school life, supporting students learning te reo, and reflecting the school's commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi. Kahu raises questions about whether all staff would support the change and what strategies could help.

Pātai Tuatahi / Question One:
Kei te tuhi a Wiremu tētahi reta ki te Tumuaki kia tono mō te reo Māori ki ngā pānui me ngā tohu katoa o te kura. He aha ōu whakaaro? Kei te whakaae, whakahē rānei? He aha ai?

Wiremu is writing to the principal to request that te reo Māori be used in all school announcements and signage. Do you agree or disagree? Explain your reason, using evidence from the text.

Write your answer in te reo Māori OR English.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- States if they agree or disagree and provides a basic reason why.
- Provides minimal links to the text.

For Merit:
- Provides a detailed description of why they agree or disagree.
- Offers detailed ideas linking back to the text.
- Provides the beginning of a detailed link to the text.

For Excellence:
- Provides a well-crafted description of why they agree or disagree with Wiremu's idea.
- Expands on their detailed opinion using relevant evidence from the text.
- Links ideas and includes personal reflections.
- Shows understanding of the meaning and purpose of the text.
- May discuss concepts such as: normalising te reo Māori in everyday school life.
- honouring Te Tiriti o Waitangi obligations.
- supporting all students to learn and engage with te reo.
- building a more inclusive school culture.

questions.text:
Pātai Tuarua / Question Two:
Ko ngā mahi a Wiremu hei waihotanga mā te kura. Ko tāu mahi te tuhi he rautaki hei whakamahinga i tō kura.

Wiremu has created a pathway for his school to follow. How would you apply Wiremu's ideas in your own school?

Write your answer in te reo Māori OR English.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Provides a limited description of what they would do with Wiremu's ideas in their school.
- States whether they like them.
- Attempts to explain how they will use the ideas.

For Merit:
- Provides a more detailed description of Wiremu's ideas and why they like them.
- Discusses how they will use them in their own school.
- Some personal reflections and ideas linking back to text.

For Excellence:
- Provides a well-developed and detailed description of Wiremu's ideas and why they value them.
- Explains with well-developed ideas how they would implement them in their school.
- Links ideas to the text, including personal reflections.
- Shows understanding of the meaning and purpose of the text.
- May discuss: introducing bilingual signage gradually.
- running te reo workshops for staff.
- student-led translation projects.
- celebrating Te Wiki o te Reo Māori.

questions.text:
Pātai Tuatoru / Question Three:
You have been selected to lead the bilingual signage project alongside Wiremu. Your task is to create an implementation plan. Identify the order of priority for the steps and explain why you have selected this order.

The steps discussed include: translating all existing signs, training staff in basic te reo pronunciation, getting student input on designs, presenting the proposal to the Board, and launching with a schoolwide celebration.

Write your answer in te reo Māori OR English.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Provides a limited description of the plan they would create.
- Brief description of how they would carry out their plan.
- Provides limited links to the text.

For Merit:
- Provides details of their plan and how they would prioritise their tasks.
- Explains an opinion of why they have ordered/prioritised their task list.
- Limited personal reflections and ideas linking back to the text.

For Excellence:
- Provides insights into their plan and it is well detailed.
- Suggests clearly why they have ordered/prioritised their task list.
- Links ideas to the text, including personal reflections.
- Shows understanding of the meaning and purpose of the text.
- May discuss: getting Board approval first to ensure authority.
- then consulting students for ownership.
- staff training before launch to ensure correct pronunciation.
- the celebration as a final step to build community support.
